analysts.summary: 44 Buy / 4 Hold (per Yahoo, Sep 7). The median target is $1,545. Recent notes cluster at $1,300-1,625: BMO $1,300 (Sep 25), Rosenblatt $1,500 (Sep 25), Wolfe $1,500 and UBS $1,625 (Sep 23). Wells Fargo cut to $1,400 from $1,525 (Sep 23), the first sign of targets flattening before the print.

bear: These are peak-cycle margins (85% gross), and management already flagged 'meaningful moderation in the rate of price increases'. Memory stocks usually peak before earnings do.
Korean peers trade at ~5x forward, so there is no multiple support if the cycle turns.
HBM share fell to 18% in Q2 as Samsung surged on HBM4.
The Taiwan union strike vote in early October could disrupt a key DRAM/HBM production hub.
Insiders sold a net $220M in 90 days with zero buyers.
Beta is 2.2 and the stock is +280% YTD; it fell 41% from its June high to its August low.
bull: Q4 guided to $50B revenue at ~86% gross margin. At that run-rate MU earns >$120 of annualized EPS against a $1,085 price.
About $100B of minimum-price multi-year agreements backed by $22B of deposits reduce the downside if spot prices fall.
Estimates keep rising: FY27 EPS went from $103 to $155 in 90 days, with 29 up-revisions vs 1 cut.
The HBM4 ramp is running twice as fast as HBM3E, and Micron's total DRAM share is at 25%, a near-record vs SK hynix.
$24B net cash and $18B+ of quarterly FCF allow bigger buybacks and dividends.
Options IV sits at a low percentile, so upside exposure is cheap.

catalysts.event: Fiscal Q4 FY26 earnings, after the close (call 4:30pm ET)
catalysts.why: Consensus is $50.82B revenue and $31.43 EPS vs a $50B/$31 guide. FQ1 FY27 guidance and commentary on contract prices and HBM4 will set the path for FY27 EPS (~$155 consensus). Management already warned of 'meaningful moderation in the rate of price increases'.

catalysts.event: Taoyuan (Taiwan) union strike vote; Micron board to approve its bonus plan
catalysts.why: Unions representing >70% of ~15,000 Taiwan staff want 15% of operating profit as bonuses. Mediation failed on Sep 22. A strike at a key DRAM/HBM site would be a supply and margin risk.

catalysts.event: Weekly options expiry just after earnings
catalysts.why: There is heavy call OI at $1,000 and $1,100. Positioning can pin or amplify the post-earnings move.

catalysts.event: HBM4 volume ramp on major customer platforms
catalysts.why: HBM4 on 1-beta DRAM is in high-volume shipment. $1B+ is booked, and management says it is ramping twice as fast as the prior generation. It is key to winning back HBM share (18% in Q2 26).

catalysts.event: Fiscal Q1 FY27 earnings (date not yet announced)
catalysts.why: The first quarter of FY27 will show whether price increases have peaked.

competition.summary: DRAM is a three-player oligopoly plus fast-growing China-based CXMT. In Q2 2026 Micron nearly caught SK hynix in total DRAM revenue share (25% vs 26%; Samsung 39%), helped by the fastest conventional DRAM growth. In HBM, Micron slipped to 18% as Samsung jumped to 33% on being first to mass-produce HBM4, while SK hynix still leads at 50%. In NAND, MU competes with SanDisk, Kioxia, Samsung and SK hynix.

CEO Sanjay Mehrotra sells 40,000 shares a month under a 10b5-1 plan. This is routine plan selling into a +280% YTD move, not a clear warning signal, but it is not supportive either.

options.expectedMove: ±$75 (~6.9%) to Oct 2 and ±$95 (~8.7%) to Oct 5, using underlying IV of 58.9%. Earnings on Sep 30 fall inside both expiries, so the real implied move is likely larger than this blended figure.
options.expiry: Oct 2 & Oct 5 2026 (nearest two with DTE >= 3). Oct 2 holds almost all the OI; Oct 5 is thin.
options.gexNote: Strikes sampled at $25 steps from $900 to $1,200 (plus Oct 5 near the money). Net dealer gamma is strongly positive at spot, about +$104M per 1% move. The largest positive GEX is at $1,100 (6,823 calls), which is the call wall. $1,000 (11,015 calls, now in the money) is the second-largest node, and $1,150/$1,200 carry 2.5k-4.2k calls. Put OI is light. The biggest put node is $900 (2,699 puts), then $950 (1,874), so the put wall is at $900. Net GEX flips negative only near ~$900, so between $1,000 and $1,100 dealer hedging should dampen moves unless earnings break the range.
options.ivNote: Underlying IV is 58.9% vs 30-day realized vol of 55.1%. The IV percentile is low: 16th over 13 weeks, 8th over 26 weeks and 13th over 52 weeks. Options are cheap vs their own history even with earnings three days out. Call OI is ~3.4x put OI near the money.
options.strategy: Educational idea, not an order. IV is cheap into a binary print, and the price sits mid fair-value band. A defined-risk structure beats adding stock here. One example: a long Oct/Nov call spread around $1,100-1,200 to play a beat-and-raise through the call wall. Another: selling $900-950 puts only if you'd be happy to own MU near the put wall and zero-gamma level. Size small. Memory stocks can move 10%+ on guidance.

politicians.summary: Members of Congress have been net buyers of MU over the past 12 months, all in small-to-mid disclosed ranges. Tony Wied's Feb 2026 buy ($250K-500K) and Cleo Fields' ($100K-250K) are the largest. The only disclosed sale was a small one by Gil Cisneros in June. PelosiTracker counts 51 disclosed trades by 20 members overall. Capitol Trades could not be read (403).

financial.note: $30.2B cash and investments vs $5.1B long-term debt; FQ3 adjusted FCF of $18.3B was a record; non-GAAP operating margin 81%.

flows.note: Institutions: $129.7B inflows vs $33.5B outflows over 12 months (MarketBeat). Insiders sold a net $220.6M in 90 days (6 sellers, 0 buyers). Options P/C OI is a call-heavy 0.29.

growth.note: FQ3 revenue +346% y/y and +74% q/q; Q4 guided to $50B (+~20% q/q). FY27 EPS consensus rose from $103 to $155 in 90 days (29 up-revisions vs 1 cut).

moat.note: One of only three scale DRAM/HBM makers, with ~$100B of minimum-price multi-year customer agreements backed by $22B in deposits. Memory is still a commodity, though, and Samsung is taking HBM share while CXMT grows fast.

momentum.note: +280% YTD and up from a $160 52-week low; $1,085 is ~14% below the $1,255 high from late June. It recovered from a $738 August low to new multi-week highs last week.

valuation.note: About 7x forward EPS and 24x TTM. Cheap on paper, but SK hynix (4.9x) and Samsung (4.7x) are cheaper, and peak-cycle earnings deserve a low multiple. The price sits inside the fair-value band.

summary: Micron is earning record, peak-cycle profits: fiscal Q3 revenue rose 346% y/y to $41.5B at an 85% gross margin, and Q4 is guided to $50B. On FY27 consensus EPS of about $155 the stock trades near 7x, which looks cheap. But memory peers SK hynix and Samsung trade near 5x, because the market discounts peak earnings. Blending peer multiples, a cycle-aware earnings-power DCF and analyst targets gives $1,010-1,345 (mid $1,180), so at $1,085 MU is fairly valued with modest upside. Hold a neutral weight into the Sep 30 earnings report: management has flagged slower price increases, the CEO keeps selling, and a Taiwan strike vote is due in early October.

valuation.method: Three methods blended (40% peers / 30% earnings power / 30% analysts). (a) Peer multiples: the pure memory peers SK hynix and Samsung trade at ~5x forward and SanDisk at 8.3x, because markets pay low multiples for peak memory earnings. Applying 6-8x to FY27 consensus EPS of ~$155 gives $930-1,240. (b) Earnings-power DCF, discounted at 11%. Bear/base: FY27 FCF/share $140, FY28 $100 as prices ease, FY29 $60, then a mid-cycle terminal of $55 EPS x 14x, plus ~$22/share net cash = ~$840. Bull: the contracted demand holds FY28 at $140, FY29 $100, then mid-cycle $80 x 15x, plus net cash = ~$1,210. (c) Analysts: 49 analysts, average $1,515, median $1,545, range $361-2,200. Blended: low $1,010, mid $1,180, high $1,345.
valuation.note: US multiples are from stockanalysis.com statistics pages read Sep 27 2026. SK hynix and Samsung multiples are from an Investing.com screen dated Aug 4 2026 (P/S shown, EV/Sales n/a) and are older. That screen showed MU at 11.2x forward before the Aug-Sep estimate upgrades. TTM P/E understates MU's earnings run-rate because the TTM window still includes pre-boom quarters.
